newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal wheat output to fall in 1997 - INE.
newsitem.headline: Portugal wheat output to fall in 1997 - INE.

text.p: Portugal's wheat output will fall to 1,760 kilos per hectare in 1997 from 1,892 last year, the National Statistics Institute (INE) said in an agriculture report.

INE's forecast for the fall was far less steep than the government's estimate that 50 to 70 percent of all winter cereal crops had been destroyed by drought, but the institute said the impact of the continuing dry weather would be reflected more clearly in its next monthly report.
"The dry, hot weather will translate into a significant reduction in output which will be visible in April's forecast," the institute said.
An Agriculture Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters the wheat shortfall would lead to a slight increase in imports.
"Because we import 80 percent of our wheat for human consumption anyway, the increase in imports won't add up to much," she said.
"There is likely to be more impact on animal feed supplies, for which we will need to find alternatives."

Deputy Secretary of State for Agriculture Carlos Cunha said on Monday that one of the worst winter droughts in the past 150 years had destroyed an estimated 50 to 70 percent of Portugal's winter cereal crops, predominantly wheat.
He said that rain last week in Portugal's southern cereal-producing Alentejo region might save pasture but not winter cereal crops, which could not now be saved regardless of weather conditions.

In 1996 Portugal produced some 415,000 tonnes of wheat, up from 360,000 tonnes the previous year. In European Union terms it is one of the smallest producers, accounting for around 0.5 percent of total wheat production.
Irrigated spring and summer cereals have not been affected by the drought because dams are full after an exceptionally wet 1995/1996 winter.
